definition_json.description: FR-BB21 (roadmap section 2.1) -- ports the categories table from c:\Users\tvolo\dev\ai-dala\BilimBaga\backend\migrations\008_categories_tags.up.sql. name is :localized_text with locales ["kk","ru","en"] and search_strategy "plain", queried: true, required: true -- the source column is a bare TEXT, but the category tree is user-facing in a trilingual product and the platform now supports per-locale generated columns (REQ-301), so this is a deliberate upgrade over the source rather than a plain transcription. track is :string, queried: true, not required -- the source column is a nullable TEXT with no CHECK; roadmap 2.1 names three built-in tracks (security, safety, loyalty) but since the source enforces no vocabulary, track stays :string rather than being promoted to :enum with a hard-coded vocabulary the source does not enforce. sort_order is :integer, queried: true, required: true, ported directly. No id, created_at, updated_at or created_by field is declared: the record subsystem (Letflow.Entities.Records) mints record identity and the event store carries the audit timeline, so declaring these here would duplicate platform-owned state inside tenant content. parent_id is :string, queried: true, not required, holding the parent category's record_id (null = root of the category tree; ports the source's categories.parent_id UUID REFERENCES categories(id)). The foreign_keys entry fk_category_parent_id promotes it to a nullable uuid self-referencing column with ON DELETE RESTRICT (decision 0025; inert on the soft-delete path, where the live rule is Letflow.Modules.Exam.AuthoringRules category_has_children). The database does not prevent cycles (as with decision 0050); the authoring write rule refuses a re-parent that would form one (parent_cycle) and a parent that does not exist (parent_not_found). definition_json.description: Core exam configuration. Ports FR-BB31 (Exam Configuration Model), source table `exams` in BilimBaga's backend/migrations/012_exams.up.sql; product spec is corporate_exam_platform_roadmap.md section 3.1, with the configuration API filters in 3.2 and the portal availability filter in 3.4 deciding which fields are queried. NOTE ON TWO DIFFERENT `description`s: this key is the definition document's own prose about the entity type; the `description` entry in `fields` below is a separate content field holding an exam's own localized description text. They are different things. FIELD-LEVEL NOTES. `title` and the `description` content field are :localized_text over ["kk","ru","en"] with search_strategy "plain": the source columns are bare TEXT with no translation table, and promoting them is a deliberate upgrade for a trilingual product, the same upgrade REQ-326 applies to category.name -- not a transcription of the source. `status`, `show_answers` and `on_tab_switch` are :enum, the direct translation of the source's Postgres ENUM types exam_status, show_answers_policy and tab_switch_action. `passing_score_pct` carries decimal_precision 5 and decimal_scale 2 ported verbatim from the source's DECIMAL(5, 2), not chosen here. `available_from` and `available_until` are queried because roadmap 3.4's portal listing filters on the availability window. OMISSIONS. No `id`, `created_at` or `updated_at` field is declared: the record subsystem owns record identity and the event store owns the timeline, so declaring them here would duplicate state the platform already holds. No `created_by` field is declared either, for the same cross-subsystem reason REQ-326 records for its own documents -- created_by references the identity subsystem's users table, which an entity fk_def cannot reach (references_entity names an entity type, not an identity-subsystem table), so an unenforced string reference would be the only option. Authorship is answered instead by the event stream's actor_id on the record's creation event. The source's idx_exams_created_by index is dropped with the column. CONSTRAINTS NOT EXPRESSIBLE HERE: the source's CHECK (time_limit_minutes > 0), CHECK (passing_score_pct BETWEEN 0 AND 100), CHECK (max_attempts > 0) and CONSTRAINT exams_availability_check are recorded in README-constraints.md in this directory, together with what is lost by relocating them.
definition_json.name: exam

definition_json.description: Who an exam is assigned to. Ports FR-BB33 (Exam Assignment), source table `exam_assignments` in BilimBaga's backend/migrations/013_exam_assignments.up.sql; product spec is corporate_exam_platform_roadmap.md section 3.3 (REQ-582, shape 1 of the open question recorded in README-constraints.md Group (iii)). `assignee_type` is :enum over exactly all, user, group and org_unit; `assignee_id` names the user, group or organisational unit and is empty for `all`. The rule 'assignee_id is required unless assignee_type is all' is not expressible in an entity definition, so a record that violates it is treated by the consumer as matching nobody. `exam_id` is :string and carries the foreign key to `exam`. `deadline` is optional. `assigned_by` is the assigning user's id as a string (the identity subsystem is not reachable by an entity foreign key). A withdrawn assignment is written as `active` false, never deleted. OMISSIONS. No `id`, `created_at` or `updated_at` field is declared: the record subsystem owns record identity and the event store owns the timeline. The type is managed by the exam module: only the exam module's authority may write its records.
definition_json.name: exam_assignment

definition_json.description: FR-BB22 (roadmap section 2.2) -- ports the questions AND question_translations tables from c:\Users\tvolo\dev\ai-dala\BilimBaga\backend\migrations\009_questions.up.sql. The two source tables collapse into this ONE entity type, which is the single most important modelling decision here: BilimBaga used a per-locale row table (question_translations) because its Postgres schema had no other way to hold multilingual text, and REQ-301's :localized_text is exactly that mechanism at the platform layer -- blob-stored with a generated column per locale when queried: true -- so question_translations has no independent existence in this pack. category_id is :string, queried: true, required: true, holding a referenced record_id; the foreign_keys entry below (fk_question_category_id) makes it a real Postgres REFERENCES. difficulty is :enum with enum_values ["easy","medium","hard"], queried: true, required: true, ported exactly from the source CHECK. type is :enum with enum_values ["single","multiple","truefalse","likert","shorttext"], queried: true, required: true, ported exactly from the source CHECK. default_locale is :string, queried: false, required: true (source default 'kk'). status is :enum with enum_values ["draft","review","active","archived"], queried: true, required: true, ported exactly from the source CHECK. version is :integer, queried: true, required: true. stem is :localized_text (source question_translations.stem) with locales ["kk","ru","en"], search_strategy "fulltext", queried: true, required: true -- fulltext because roadmap 2.3's question list is searchable and 2.5's duplicate detection is trigram similarity over stems; this is the one field in this pack where search strategy is load-bearing rather than incidental, which is why it differs from category.name's "plain" strategy. explanation is :localized_text (source question_translations.explanation, nullable) with locales ["kk","ru","en"], search_strategy "plain", queried: false, required: false. Foreign keys: fk_question_category_id (field "category_id", references_entity "category"). Indexes: idx_question_status over status and idx_question_category_id over category_id (mirroring the source's idx_questions_status and idx_questions_category_id), plus idx_question_type over type because roadmap 2.3's list endpoint filters on it. No id, created_at, updated_at field is declared: the record subsystem mints record identity and the event store carries the audit timeline, so declaring these here would duplicate platform-owned state inside tenant content. created_by UUID NOT NULL REFERENCES users(id) is DROPPED: an entity definition's fk_def can only reference another entity type in the same tenant's entity subsystem (references_entity is resolved through the promoted-column tables), and identity.users is a different subsystem that no fk_def can span. What replaces it: authorship is already captured by the event store -- every Letflow.Entities.Records write carries actor_id into the ENTITY_RECORD_CREATED event -- so "who authored this question" is answerable from the event stream without a duplicated, unenforceable column; no plain :string created_by field holding an unenforced user id is declared. parent_id is :string, queried: true, not required, holding the predecessor question's record_id (version lineage, ports the source's questions.parent_id UUID REFERENCES questions(id): "parent_id links a new version to its predecessor; only the latest version is active"; null = first version). The foreign_keys entry fk_question_parent_id promotes it to a nullable uuid self-referencing column with ON DELETE RESTRICT (decision 0025; inert on the soft-delete path, where the live rule is Letflow.Modules.Exam.AuthoringRules question_has_children). The authoring surface refuses a parent that does not exist (parent_not_found); the lineage rules (one successor per version, version ordering, one active version per lineage) are REQ-586 part B. Indexes: idx_question_parent_id over parent_id.
definition_json.name: question

definition_json.description: FR-BB22 (roadmap section 2.2) -- ports the answer_options AND answer_translations tables from c:\Users\tvolo\dev\ai-dala\BilimBaga\backend\migrations\009_questions.up.sql. The same two-tables-into-one collapse as question.json, for the same reason: BilimBaga used a per-locale row table (answer_translations) because its Postgres schema had no other way to hold multilingual text, and REQ-301's :localized_text is exactly that mechanism at the platform layer, so answer_translations has no independent existence in this pack. question_id is :string, queried: true, required: true. sort_order is :integer, queried: true, required: true. is_correct is :boolean, queried: true, required: true (source default FALSE). likert_weight is :decimal with decimal_precision: 5, decimal_scale: 2, queried: false, required: false -- both numbers are ported directly from the source's DECIMAL(5,2), not chosen independently. likert_polarity is :enum with enum_values ["positive","negative"], queried: false, required: false, ported from the source CHECK. text is :localized_text (source answer_translations.text) with locales ["kk","ru","en"], search_strategy "plain", queried: true, required: true. Foreign keys: fk_answer_option_question_id (field "question_id", references_entity "question"). Indexes: idx_answer_option_question_id over question_id, mirroring the source's idx_answer_options_question_id. is_correct and field-level redaction: is_correct is the field a candidate must never see, and this is exactly what Letflow.Entities.Query.FieldGrants (REQ-231) -- field-level redaction that already exists -- is meant to govern. This pack does not configure a field grant; it only ensures is_correct is a first-class promoted field on its own record, so that redaction is expressible at all, which it would not be if answer options were nested inside the question's blob as a JSON array. This is the reason answer_option is authored as a separate entity type rather than a JSON array on question. No id, created_at, updated_at or created_by field is declared: the record subsystem mints record identity and the event store carries the audit timeline, so declaring these here would duplicate platform-owned state inside tenant content.

definition_json.description: FR-BB22 (roadmap section 2.3, the tag-association endpoints) -- ports the question_tags table from c:\Users\tvolo\dev\ai-dala\BilimBaga\backend\migrations\009_questions.up.sql. This is authored as a join entity type, per docs/anti-patterns.md's "Modelling many-to-many as an array of references on the parent record" entry: an earlier draft giving question a tag_ids array was rejected because it is unindexed by default without an explicit GIN index, has nowhere to put join attributes, and is invisible to Letflow.Entities.Query.FieldGrants, which redacts at field granularity on a record and cannot see values inside an array on someone else's row. No tag_ids field or any other array-of-references field is declared anywhere in this pack. Instead question_tag is an ordinary entity type whose promoted columns are two foreign keys: question_id :string, queried: true, required: true, and tag_id :string, queried: true, required: true. Foreign keys: fk_question_tag_question_id (field "question_id", references_entity "question") and fk_question_tag_tag_id (field "tag_id", references_entity "tag"). Constraints: uq_question_tag_question_id_tag_id, type "unique", fields ["question_id","tag_id"] -- this expresses the source's composite PRIMARY KEY on (question_id, tag_id). Indexes: idx_question_tag_tag_id over tag_id, mirroring the source's 010_question_tags_tag_id_index.up.sql reverse-lookup index. This shape is also what Letflow.Entities.Query.Compiler's through many-to-many join (REQ-300) requires: lib/letflow/design/req300-query-joins.md section 4 describes a join entity owning foreign keys to both sides as the shape it resolves, so authoring question_tag this way is what makes "list the questions carrying tag X" a compilable query rather than an application-level fetch. No id, created_at, updated_at or created_by field is declared: the record subsystem mints record identity and the event store carries the audit timeline, so declaring these here would duplicate platform-owned state inside tenant content.
definition_json.name: question_tag

definition_json.description: One question-selection rule for an exam -- either a random pool draw or a manual pin list. Ports FR-BB31 (Exam Configuration Model), source table `exam_question_rules` in BilimBaga's backend/migrations/012_exams.up.sql; product spec is corporate_exam_platform_roadmap.md section 3.1. THE tag_ids JSONB COLUMN IS DELIBERATELY REMODELLED, NOT TRANSCRIBED. The source table carries `tag_ids JSONB NOT NULL DEFAULT '[]'::jsonb`, an array of tag references held on the parent row. That column is deliberately NOT ported as a field here. Carrying it forward as a :json field would be exactly the shape docs/anti-patterns.md's "Modelling many-to-many as an array of references on the parent record" entry records as rejected: unindexed by default and so degrading to a scan, with nowhere to put join attributes, and invisible to Letflow.Entities.Query.FieldGrants (REQ-231), which redacts at field granularity on a record and cannot field-redact values inside an array on another row. The rule-to-tag relationship is instead modelled as an ordinary join entity type, exam_question_rule_tag, in this same directory -- an entity whose promoted columns are two foreign keys with a constraint_def of type "unique" over the pair, which is the correct alternative that anti-pattern entry names and the shape Letflow.Entities.Query.Compiler's through join (REQ-300) resolves against. This is a deliberate remodelling of the source schema, not a transcription of it. FIELD-LEVEL NOTES. `difficulty` is :string and deliberately NOT :enum. The source column is a bare nullable TEXT with no CHECK, unlike questions.difficulty, which does carry one; tightening a column the source itself left loose would invent a constraint the port has no evidence for, so the asymmetry between this field and question.difficulty is deliberate rather than an oversight. `section_id` is required false because the source is a nullable FK with ON DELETE SET NULL; `category_id` is likewise a nullable source FK. `mode` is :enum, the direct translation of the source's question_selection_mode Postgres ENUM. `category_id` references the `category` entity type authored by REQ-326. The source's UNIQUE (exam_id, sort_order) is expressible exactly and is declared below. OMISSIONS. No `id`, `created_at` or `updated_at` field is declared: the record subsystem owns record identity and the event store owns the timeline. CONSTRAINTS NOT EXPRESSIBLE HERE: the source's CHECK (count > 0) and CHECK (sort_order >= 0) are single-column range checks with no entity-definition expression; both are recorded in README-constraints.md in this directory, along with the fact that relocating them loses database-level enforcement.
definition_json.name: exam_question_rule

definition_json.description: Join entity binding one exam question-selection rule to one tag it draws from. THIS ENTITY TYPE HAS NO SOURCE TABLE. It does not port a table from BilimBaga's backend/migrations/012_exams.up.sql; it REPLACES the `tag_ids JSONB NOT NULL DEFAULT '[]'::jsonb` column on that migration's `exam_question_rules` table. It belongs to FR-BB31 (Exam Configuration Model) and corporate_exam_platform_roadmap.md section 3.1 by way of the rule it decomposes. The remodelling is deliberate: an array of references held on the parent row is the shape docs/anti-patterns.md's "Modelling many-to-many as an array of references on the parent record" entry records as rejected (unindexed by default, nowhere to put join attributes, invisible to Letflow.Entities.Query.FieldGrants), and the correct alternative that entry names is exactly this -- an ordinary entity type whose promoted columns are two foreign keys, with a constraint_def of type "unique" over the pair. This is the same join shape REQ-326 authors for question_tag and for the same reason: it is what Letflow.Entities.Query.Compiler's through join (REQ-300) resolves against. `tag_id` references the `tag` entity type authored by REQ-326. OMISSIONS. No `id`, `created_at` or `updated_at` field is declared: the record subsystem owns record identity and the event store owns the timeline. This entity type carries no CHECK constraint from any source, having no source table.
definition_json.name: exam_question_rule_tag

definition_json.description: The explicit pin list of questions used when an exam question-selection rule's mode is "manual". Ports FR-BB31 (Exam Configuration Model), source table `exam_manual_questions` in BilimBaga's backend/migrations/012_exams.up.sql; product spec is corporate_exam_platform_roadmap.md section 3.1. FIELD-LEVEL NOTES. `question_id` references the `question` entity type authored by REQ-326. The source table has no surrogate id: its identity is the composite PRIMARY KEY (rule_id, question_id), which is expressible exactly and is declared below as a constraints entry of type "unique" over ["rule_id", "question_id"] -- the platform's own record identity supplies the surrogate key the source did not have. NAMING NOTE: this document's fk on rule_id and its unique over [rule_id, question_id] both start from rule_id, so an unprefixed naming convention would collide -- validator.ex's Rule 2 (duplicate_name_violations/1) concatenates foreign_keys and constraints into ONE shared uniqueness scope. The fk_/uq_ prefixes keep that shared scope collision-free by construction. OMISSIONS. No `id`, `created_at` or `updated_at` field is declared: the record subsystem owns record identity and the event store owns the timeline. CONSTRAINT NOT EXPRESSIBLE HERE: the source's CHECK (sort_order >= 0) is a single-column range check with no entity-definition expression; it is recorded in README-constraints.md in this directory, along with the fact that relocating it loses database-level enforcement.

definition_json.description: FR-BB35 -- ports exam_sessions from c:\Users\tvolo\dev\ai-dala\BilimBaga\backend\migrations\014_exam_sessions.up.sql, with status widened by 015_session_tables.up.sql's ALTER TYPE. Product spec: corporate_exam_platform_roadmap.md section 3.6. FIELD-LEVEL NOTES. exam_id is :string, queried: true, required: true, with foreign_keys entry fk_session_exam_id making it a real Postgres REFERENCES against the exam entity type. user_id is :string, queried: true, required: true, but carries NO fk_def: users live in the identity subsystem, and references_entity names an entity type in the tenant's own entity subsystem, not an identity-subsystem table -- the same reasoning REQ-326 recorded for created_by. status is :enum with FOUR values in_progress, submitted, auto_submitted, grading_pending; the source's 014 migration declares only the first three, and grading_pending was added afterward by 015's `ALTER TYPE session_status ADD VALUE IF NOT EXISTS 'grading_pending'` -- the fourth value is not in 014, it is a 015 addition. seed is :integer (source BIGINT), queried: false, required: true; its purpose is reproducibility of the shuffled question set derived at session creation, per roadmap 3.5, not a value ever filtered on. started_at is :datetime, queried: false, required: true. expires_at is :datetime, queried: true, required: true -- it MUST be queried: true because REQ-331's auto-submit sweep locates expired sessions by scanning on this field, standing in for the source's partial index idx_exam_sessions_expires_status; a definition where expires_at is not queried would leave that sweep with no indexed predicate to run against. submitted_at is :datetime, queried: false, required: false (source nullable, set only on submission). score_pct is :decimal with decimal_precision 5 and decimal_scale 2, ported verbatim from the source's DECIMAL(5,2), queried: false, required: false. passed is :boolean, queried: false, required: true (source NOT NULL DEFAULT FALSE). Foreign keys: fk_session_exam_id (field exam_id, references_entity exam). Indexes: idx_session_exam_user over (exam_id, user_id) and idx_session_user_exam_status over (user_id, exam_id, status), both mirroring the source's idx_exam_sessions_exam_user and idx_exam_sessions_user_exam_status; idx_session_expires_status over (expires_at, status) stands in for the source's partial index idx_exam_sessions_expires_status WHERE status = 'in_progress' -- Letflow's index_def has no WHERE clause, so this becomes a full composite index rather than a partial one; the auto-submit sweep still uses it, just over a wider row set than the source scanned. OMISSIONS. No id, created_at or updated_at field is declared: the record subsystem owns record identity and the event store owns the timeline, so declaring them here would duplicate platform-owned state. No created_by field is declared for the same reason -- this table has no created_by column in the source anyway; user_id already plays that role and is handled above. CONSTRAINTS NOT EXPRESSIBLE HERE: the source's exam_sessions_score_range CHECK (score_pct BETWEEN 0 AND 100) and exam_sessions_expires_after_start CHECK (expires_at > started_at), both added by 015, are relocated to priv/packs/bilimbaga/entity_definitions/README-constraints.md with what is lost by relocating them. ON DELETE: exam_id's fk_def promotes to a Postgres FK that lib/letflow/entities/definition/ddl.ex:675 emits as ON DELETE RESTRICT unconditionally (decision 0025 sub-question 1), which diverges from the source's ON DELETE CASCADE on exam_sessions.exam_id -- see the ON DELETE table in README-constraints.md. user_id's source column is also ON DELETE CASCADE, but carries no Letflow fk_def at all (identity subsystem), so there is no Letflow FK for it to diverge from; it is still recorded in the README's table for completeness. EXAM SNAPSHOT (GH #2682 / REQ-511). exam_snapshot is :json, queried: false, required: false: the scoring-relevant exam content frozen when the session starts (answer key, question types, passing threshold, certificate facts), with a SHA-256 digest and a random nonce. Scoring and the autosave shape check read only this snapshot, never the live authoring rows. It carries the answer key, so it is restricted by field (entity_field_restrictions) and never appears in a candidate-facing response. TIMESTAMPTZ: started_at, expires_at, submitted_at (and the dropped created_at) were all TIMESTAMPTZ in the source; ddl.ex:318 maps :datetime to timestamp(6) without time zone, dropping the offset on all of them -- recorded in README-constraints.md, singling out expires_at because REQ-331's sweep compares it against now across tenants.
definition_json.name: session

definition_json.description: FR-BB35 -- ports session_questions from c:\Users\tvolo\dev\ai-dala\BilimBaga\backend\migrations\014_exam_sessions.up.sql AS RESHAPED by 015_session_tables.up.sql's AC-2 ALTERs. Product spec: corporate_exam_platform_roadmap.md section 3.6. FIELD-LEVEL NOTES. session_id is :string, queried: true, required: true, foreign_keys entry fk_session_question_session_id against session. question_id is :string, queried: true, required: true, foreign_keys entry fk_session_question_question_id against question. sort_order is :integer, queried: false, required: true (source CHECK sort_order >= 0, relocated -- see below). options_order is :json, queried: false, required: true -- an ordered array of option UUIDs; Rule 3 forbids a :json field being queried and nothing here needs to filter on it. options_order materialises a RESOLVED, SHUFFLED question set fixed at session creation, which combined with session.seed is what makes a session's question order reproducible. question_version_id is :string, queried: false, required: false (source nullable UUID added by 015's ALTER TABLE ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS question_version_id). CONSTRAINT: constraints entry uq_session_question_session_id_question_id, type unique, over (session_id, question_id) -- this expresses 015's composite PRIMARY KEY (session_id, question_id) the convention-compliant way, without declaring a primary key, because the record subsystem already owns record identity; the same convention REQ-326 and REQ-327 established for their own join entities. 015 also DROPPED the surrogate id column and the old UNIQUE (session_id, sort_order), replacing them with this composite PK -- the unique constraint above is the accurate port of the CURRENT (post-015) shape, not of 014's original UNIQUE (session_id, sort_order), which no longer exists in the source. ON DELETE, DELIBERATE SOURCE CHANGE: 015 deliberately changed question_id's FK from ON DELETE CASCADE (014's original) to ON DELETE RESTRICT, so that deleting a question can no longer silently rewrite a sat exam's resolved question set. Letflow reaches the same RESTRICT behaviour for free, because lib/letflow/entities/definition/ddl.ex:675 emits a fixed, unconditional ON DELETE RESTRICT on every promoted FK regardless of what fk_def declares (decision 0025 sub-question 1) -- fk_def itself (lib/letflow/entities/definition.ex) has no on_delete key at all. session_id's FK, by contrast, is CASCADE in the source and RESTRICT in Letflow, a genuine divergence -- see the seven-row ON DELETE table in README-constraints.md, which covers both FKs on this entity type. OMISSIONS. No id, created_at or updated_at field is declared, for the usual cross-subsystem reason: the record subsystem owns identity and the event store owns the timeline. No created_by field is declared -- the source table never had one. CONSTRAINTS NOT EXPRESSIBLE HERE: the source's sort_order CHECK (sort_order >= 0) is relocated to README-constraints.md with what is lost by relocating it. TIMESTAMPTZ: this entity type has no datetime column (options_order is JSON, not a timestamp), so the TIMESTAMPTZ-to-naive divergence recorded in README-constraints.md does not apply here; it is listed there against the four other documents' datetime columns.
definition_json.name: session_question

definition_json.description: FR-BB36 AC-5 -- ports session_answers from c:\Users\tvolo\dev\ai-dala\BilimBaga\backend\migrations\015_session_tables.up.sql. Product spec: corporate_exam_platform_roadmap.md section 3.6. FIELD-LEVEL NOTES. session_id is :string, queried: true, required: true, foreign_keys entry fk_session_answer_session_id against session. question_id is :string, queried: true, required: true, foreign_keys entry fk_session_answer_question_id against question. selected_option_ids is :json, queried: false, required: false -- an array of selected option UUIDs; Rule 3 forbids a :json field being queried and nothing needs to filter on it. text_answer is :string, queried: false, required: false (source nullable TEXT) -- this is a candidate's own free-text answer, NOT localized content: it is not authored prose meant to be shown in multiple locales, it is a per-answer string keyed to one candidate's submission, so :string is correct here and :localized_text is not, unlike question.stem or exam.title. saved_at is :datetime, queried: false, required: true (source DEFAULT NOW()). time_spent_seconds is :integer, queried: false, required: true (source DEFAULT 0, CHECK time_spent_seconds >= 0, relocated below). CONSTRAINT: constraints entry uq_session_answer_session_id_question_id, type unique, over (session_id, question_id) -- this expresses the source's UNIQUE (session_id, question_id), which is the upsert key the source's SaveAnswer path relies on to overwrite a candidate's prior answer to the same question rather than duplicate a row; it also matches the composite-natural-key convention REQ-326/REQ-327 established, though here the source itself used UNIQUE rather than a composite PK. ON DELETE: session_id's FK is CASCADE in the source and RESTRICT in Letflow (ddl.ex:675, decision 0025) -- a divergence; question_id's FK is RESTRICT in the source already, so Letflow's fixed RESTRICT matches. Both rows are in the seven-row table in README-constraints.md. OMISSIONS. No id, created_at or updated_at field is declared, for the usual cross-subsystem reason. No created_by field is declared -- the source table has none; the answering candidate is already session_id -> session.user_id, and the event stream's actor_id answers who wrote this specific record. CONSTRAINTS NOT EXPRESSIBLE HERE: the source's time_spent_seconds CHECK (time_spent_seconds >= 0) is relocated to README-constraints.md with what is lost by relocating it. TIMESTAMPTZ: saved_at was TIMESTAMPTZ in the source; ddl.ex:318 maps :datetime to timestamp(6) without time zone, dropping the offset -- recorded in README-constraints.md alongside the other datetime columns; saved_at does not carry the same correctness stakes as session.expires_at, but the mapping is identical and is recorded there rather than treated as a separate note.

definition_json.description: FR-BB36 AC-4 -- ports tab_switch_events from c:\Users\tvolo\dev\ai-dala\BilimBaga\backend\migrations\015_session_tables.up.sql, PLUS ONE DELIBERATE ADDITION beyond the source schema. Product spec: corporate_exam_platform_roadmap.md section 3.6. READ THIS IN FULL BEFORE TREATING THIS AS A STRAIGHT PORT -- IT IS NOT ONE. NAMING: this entity type is named session_event, not tab_switch_event, and the reason rests entirely on the added event_type field below, NOT on any claim about what tab_switch_events itself stores: this entity records all three signal types service.go's ReportEvent accepts (tab_switch, blur, fullscreen_exit), only one of which is literally a tab switch, so tab_switch_event would be a narrower name than the entity's own contents warrant. The source table tab_switch_events stores none of the three signal-type strings -- see OMISSIONS below. THE SOURCE TABLE, VERBATIM (015_session_tables.up.sql AC-4 block): `id UUID PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(), session_id UUID NOT NULL REFERENCES exam_sessions(id) ON DELETE CASCADE, occurred_at TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT NOW(), action_taken TEXT NOT NULL` -- exactly four columns, and event_type is not one of them. FIELD-LEVEL NOTES (the three ported fields). session_id is :string, queried: true, required: true, foreign_keys entry fk_session_event_session_id against session. occurred_at is :datetime, queried: true, required true (source DEFAULT NOW()) -- queried because a proctoring review needs to order and filter a session's events by time. action_taken is :enum with values log, warn, submit (source bare TEXT, but service.go's ReportEvent only ever writes one of these three, driven off the exam's on_tab_switch policy -- see the derivation note below). OMISSIONS. tab_switch_events has no event_type column, no id column is declared here (usual cross-subsystem reason), and no created_at/updated_at/created_by field is declared either. ADDITIONS -- event_type IS A DELIBERATE ADDITION TO THE SOURCE SCHEMA, NOT A PORT. event_type is :enum with values tab_switch, blur, fullscreen_exit, queried: false, required: true. The source VALIDATES this exact value and then THROWS IT AWAY: service.go:530's ReportEvent checks `!validEventTypes[input.Type]` against a validEventTypes map admitting exactly tab_switch, blur and fullscreen_exit, rejecting anything else with ErrInvalidEventType -- but the INSERT that follows, repository.go:705-709's InsertTabSwitchEvent, is `INSERT INTO tab_switch_events (session_id, occurred_at, action_taken) VALUES ($1, NOW(), $2)`, binding only session_id and action_taken; the eventType parameter passed into InsertTabSwitchEvent is never bound to anything and is dropped on the floor. After a session ends, the source's own data cannot distinguish an alt-tab from a fullscreen exit -- both leave identical rows differing only in whatever action_taken happened to be at that moment. Persisting event_type here anyway is the right call despite reproducing more than the source stores: the three signal types carry materially different evidentiary weight in a proctoring dispute (a candidate briefly alt-tabbing reads very differently from repeatedly exiting fullscreen), an integrity record that can only say WHAT ACTION WAS TAKEN but never WHAT THE CANDIDATE ACTUALLY DID is close to useless for the purpose this table exists to serve, and the column costs exactly one enum on a row that is already being written on every event. Reproducing the source's bug (discarding a value it already validated) is not fidelity; it is carrying forward a defect. Foreign keys: fk_session_event_session_id (field session_id, references_entity session). Indexes: idx_session_event_session_id over session_id, mirroring the source's idx_tab_switch_events_session_id. ENFORCEMENT NOTE, NOT SETTLED HERE: action_taken is DERIVED FROM THE EXAM'S on_tab_switch CONFIGURATION AND NEVER FROM THE REQUEST BODY -- service.go's ReportEvent, AC-10 (service.go:554-555, `action_taken is derived from the exam config, not the request body`), fetches the exam's on_tab_switch policy via GetExamConfig and passes cfg.OnTabSwitch, not any client-supplied field, into InsertTabSwitchEvent. This entity definition does not itself enforce that derivation -- it only declares the field shapes -- so this is stated here as a REQ-333 enforcement obligation on whichever write path implements ReportEvent's equivalent, and must not be read as permitting a client-supplied action_taken value at the record-write layer. ON DELETE: session_id's FK is CASCADE in the source and RESTRICT in Letflow (ddl.ex:675, decision 0025) -- a divergence, one of the five in the seven-row table in README-constraints.md. TIMESTAMPTZ: occurred_at was TIMESTAMPTZ in the source; ddl.ex:318 maps :datetime to timestamp(6) without time zone, dropping the offset -- recorded in README-constraints.md alongside session.expires_at and the other datetime columns.
definition_json.name: session_event

definition_json.description: FR-BB311 -- ports session_question_scores from c:\Users\tvolo\dev\ai-dala\BilimBaga\backend\migrations\016_session_question_scores.up.sql. Product spec: corporate_exam_platform_roadmap.md section 3.6. FIELD-LEVEL NOTES. session_id is :string, queried: true, required: true, foreign_keys entry fk_session_question_score_session_id against session. question_id is :string, queried: true, required: true, foreign_keys entry fk_session_question_score_question_id against question. score is :decimal with decimal_precision 6 and decimal_scale 4, ported verbatim from the source's DECIMAL(6,4), queried: false, required: true (source DEFAULT 0). max_score is :decimal with decimal_precision 6 and decimal_scale 4, same source type, queried: false, required: true (source DEFAULT 1). grading_status is :enum with values graded, pending_manual, ai_graded, queried: true, required: true (source DEFAULT 'graded'). CONSTRAINT: constraints entry uq_session_question_score_session_id_question_id, type unique, over (session_id, question_id) -- this expresses the source's composite PRIMARY KEY (session_id, question_id) without declaring a primary key, because the record subsystem owns record identity; the same convention session_question and session_answer follow above. INDEX: idx_session_question_score_session_grading_status over (session_id, grading_status) stands in for the source's partial index idx_session_question_scores_pending ON session_question_scores(session_id) WHERE grading_status = 'pending_manual' -- Letflow's index_def has no WHERE clause, so this is a FULL composite index over every grading_status value, not a partial index limited to pending_manual rows; it is a difference, not an equivalent, though it still serves the same query shape (find a session's pending-manual rows) at the cost of indexing the other two statuses as well. ON DELETE: session_id's FK is CASCADE in the source and RESTRICT in Letflow (ddl.ex:675, decision 0025) -- a divergence; question_id's FK is RESTRICT in the source already, so Letflow's fixed RESTRICT matches. Both rows are in the seven-row table in README-constraints.md. OMISSIONS. No id, created_at or updated_at field is declared, for the usual cross-subsystem reason -- the source table in fact has no id or timestamp columns of its own either, only the composite PK. No created_by field is declared -- grading is attributable via the event stream's actor_id on whichever record write applied it (manual grading or the AI grading pipeline), not a column on this row. This entity type has no datetime column, so the TIMESTAMPTZ divergence recorded in README-constraints.md does not apply here.

definition_json.description: REQ-355 -- ports FR-BB43 (Certificate Generation), source table `certificates` from c:\Users\tvolo\dev\ai-dala\BilimBaga\backend\migrations\019_certificates.up.sql, service behaviour from backend/internal/certificates/service.go's GetOrCreate. Bucket A by the same reasoning REQ-329's five session entity types recorded: this is a declarative record shape with no execution semantics of its own -- the eligibility/idempotency/snapshot LOGIC that decides when and how a row here gets written lives in the bucket-C context module lib/letflow/exam/certificate.ex, exactly mirroring how session.json (data) is paired with Letflow.Exam.Session (behaviour). FIELD-LEVEL NOTES. session_id is :string, queried: true, required: true, with a real fk_def (fk_certificate_session_id) against the session entity type -- the source's session_id UUID NOT NULL UNIQUE REFERENCES exam_sessions(id). issued_at is :datetime, queried: false, required: true (source TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT NOW(), stamped by the context module at issuance, never left to a storage-layer default). candidate_name is :string, queried: false, required: true -- the direct port of the source's employee_name TEXT NOT NULL (Letflow's identity subsystem has no per-tenant employee concept, so this stores the issuing candidate's Letflow.Identity.User.display_name at issuance time, captured into this record for the same reason the branding snapshot is captured: so a later change to the candidate's own display_name does not alter an already-issued certificate). exam_title is :json, queried: false, required: true -- a DELIBERATE UPGRADE over the source's exam_title TEXT NOT NULL, storing the exam's full :localized_text map (all locales) rather than a single string, the same upgrade REQ-327's exam.json already made for exam.title itself; carrying the whole map here (not one flattened locale) is what lets a later renderer (REQ-356) pick the right locale without re-reading the live exam record. score_pct is :decimal with decimal_precision 5 and decimal_scale 2, ported verbatim from the source's DECIMAL(5,2), queried: false, required: true. branding_snapshot is :json, queried: false, required: true -- has NO source column (FR-BB43's TemplateSnapshot was a separate JSONB column, template_snapshot, holding the same idea under a different name); this is the field FR-BB43 AC-9 depends on: the context module reads lib/letflow/routers/tenant_config.ex's branding_from_settings/1 exactly once, at first issuance, and stores its full three-key map here verbatim -- a later branding change never touches an already-issued row because nothing here re-reads live branding. OMISSIONS, deliberate and matching every other document in this directory. No id, created_at or updated_at field is declared: the record subsystem (Letflow.Entities.Records) owns record identity and the event store owns the timeline. No created_by field: the issuing candidate is already named by session_id -> session.user_id, and by this record's own creation event's actor_id, so a third copy would be redundant. NOT PORTED, out of this requirement's scope (see lib/letflow/exam/certificate.ex's own moduledoc for the full accounting): verification_code (REQ-357's public-verification scope, not this requirement's) and template_snapshot's PDF-rendering consumer (REQ-356's scope) -- this document intentionally has no verification_code field, so a document expecting one is looking at the wrong requirement. IDEMPOTENCY, NOT EXPRESSED AS A `constraints` UNIQUE ENTRY HERE, EXPLAINED: the source's guarantee is `session_id UUID NOT NULL UNIQUE` plus `INSERT ... ON CONFLICT (session_id) DO NOTHING`. This document deliberately declares NO `constraints` entry for session_id, even though Letflow.Entities.Definition's constraint_def type could express a :unique constraint over ["session_id"] -- because doing so would trigger ISS-0648's automatic column-promotion-on-activation (a real per-entity-type SQL table plus a real Postgres UNIQUE constraint on a promoted column), which is materially heavier machinery than this record shape needs and would silently answer the very A/B question this requirement's own REVIEWER rule-2 sign-off is supposed to weigh (whether a certificate needs anything beyond ordinary entity-record semantics). Letflow.Exam.Certificate's own moduledoc records the idempotency mechanism actually used instead -- a deterministic Letflow.Entities.Records.create_record/2 idempotency_key derived from session_id, backed by the REAL, ALREADY-UNIQUE-INDEXED event_idempotency table every entity-record write already goes through -- and states its guarantee level precisely.
definition_json.name: certificate
